source_text:
Ὁρᾶτε, ἀγαπητοί, μὴ αἱ εὐεργεσίαι αὐτοῦ αἱ πολλαὶ γένωνται εἰς κρίμα ἡμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ ἀξίως αὐτοῦ πολιτευόμενοι τὰ καλὰ καὶ εὐάρεστα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ποιῶμεν μεθ̓ ὁμονοίας.
λέγει γάρ που: Πνεῦμα κυρίου λύχνος ἐρευνῶν τὰ ταμιεῖα τῆς γαστρός:
ἴδωμεν. πῶς ἐγγύς ἐστιν, καὶ ὅτι οὐδὲν λέληθεν αὐτὸν τῶν ἐννοιῶν ἡμῶν οὐδὲ τῶν διαλογισμῶν ὧν ποιούμεθα:
δίκαιον οὖν ἐστὶν μὴ λειποτακτεῖν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ.
μᾶλλον ἀνθρώποις ἄφροσι καὶ ἀνοήτοις καὶ ἐπαιρομένοις καὶ ἐγκαυχωμένοις ἐν ἀλαζονείᾳ τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν προσκόψωμεν ἢ τῷ θεῷ.
τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, οὗ τὸ αἷμα ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐδόθη, ἐντραπῶμεν, τοὺς προηγουμένους ἡμῶν αἰδεσθῶμεν, τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τιμήσωμεν, τοὺς νέους παιδεύσωμεν τὴν παιδείαν τοῦ φόβου τοῦ θεοῦ, τὰς γυναῖκας ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀγαθὸν διορθωσώμεθα.
τὸ ἀξιαγάπητον τῆς ἁγνείας ἦθος ἐνδειξάσθωσαν, τὸ ἀκέραιον τῆς πραΰτητος αὐτῶν βούλημα ἀποδειξάτωσαν, τὸ ἐπιεικὲς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτῶν διὰ τῆς σιγῆς φανερὸν ποιησάτωσαν, τὴν ἀγάπην αὐτῶν μὴ κατὰ προσκλίσεις, ἀλλὰ πᾶσιν τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸν θεὸν ὁσίως ἴσην παρεχέτωσαν.
τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ παιδείας μεταλαμβανέτωσαν: μαθέτωσαν, τί ταπεινοφροσύνη παρὰ θεῷ ἰσχύει, τί ἀγάπη ἁγνὴ παρὰ θεῷ δύναται, πῶς ὁ φόβος αὐτοῦ καλὸς καὶ μέγας καὶ σώζων πάντας τοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ ὁσίως ἀναστρεφομένους ἐν καθαρᾷ διανοίᾳ.
ἐρευνητὴς γάρ ἐστιν ἐννοιῶν καὶ ἐνθυμήσεων: οὗ ἡ πνοὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐστίν, καὶ ὅταν θέλῃ, ἀνελεῖ αὐτήν.
thought_title: Live worthily before the all-seeing God
orientation: The Roman church, having just praised God's ordered creation, now turns to exhort the Corinthians directly about their conduct before God.
pass_a_gloss: See, beloved, that his many benefits do not become for judgment to us, if not worthily of him conducting ourselves we do the good and pleasing things before him with harmony. For he says somewhere: The spirit of the Lord is a lamp searching the inner chambers of the belly. Let us see how near he is, and that nothing is hidden from him of our thoughts nor of the reasonings which we make. Right therefore it is that we do not desert from his will. Rather let us offend foolish and senseless and puffed-up and boasting men in the arrogance of their word than God. Let us reverence the Lord Jesus Christ, whose blood was given for us, let us respect our leaders, let us honor the elders, let us train the young in the training of the fear of God, let us set our wives straight toward the good. Let them display the lovable character of purity, let them show forth the sincere purpose of their gentleness, let them make the mildness of their tongue manifest through silence, let them provide their love not according to partialities but equally to all who fear God in holiness. Let our children partake of the training in Christ; let them learn what humility is strong for with God, what pure love is able to do with God, how the fear of him is good and great and saves all who in it conduct themselves holily in a pure mind. For he is a searcher of thoughts and reflections; his breath is in us, and when he wills, he will take it away.

choices.why: Keeps the dative of disadvantage and the sense that God's benefits become a liability if received unworthily.
The verb means living as a citizen; 'conducting ourselves' preserves the ethical force without importing a political metaphor.

choices.english: the inner chambers of the belly
choices.why: Literal rendering of the LXX phrase; 'inner chambers' keeps the architectural metaphor of hidden storage rooms.
rejected: the secret places of the belly

choices.why: The military metaphor of abandoning one's post is central to the argument about not leaving God's will.
The verb means to strike against; 'offend' captures the sense of giving offense to humans rather than God.
The noun means leaning or inclination; the plural suggests favoritism, which the context explicitly contrasts with equal love for all.

bible_refs.note: Πνεῦμα κυρίου λύχνος ἐρευνῶν τὰ ταμιεῖα τῆς γαστρός

pass_b_english: Take care, beloved, that God's many benefits do not become judgment for us. This will happen if we fail to live worthily of him and to do what is good and pleasing in his sight with harmony.
For he says somewhere: "The spirit of the Lord is a lamp searching the inner chambers of the belly" (Proverbs 20:27).
Let us consider how near he is, and that none of our thoughts or the reasonings we make escapes his notice.
It is right, then, that we should not desert his will.
Let us offend foolish and thoughtless people, people who exalt themselves and boast in the arrogance of their words, rather than God.

Let us reverence the Lord Jesus Christ, whose blood was given for us. Let us respect our leaders. Let us honor the elders. Let us train the young in the discipline of the fear of God. Let us guide our wives toward what is good.

Let them display the lovable character of purity. Let them demonstrate the sincere will of their gentleness. Let them make the moderation of their tongue evident through silence. Let them offer their love not according to partialities, but equally to all who fear God in holiness.

Let our children share in the discipline that is in Christ. Let them learn how much humility prevails with God, how much pure love can accomplish with God, how the fear of him is good and great and saves all who conduct themselves in it in holiness with a pure mind.
For he is the searcher of thoughts and reflections. His breath is in us, and when he wills, he will take it away.

problems.why: 'ἐνθυμήσεις' means 'thoughts, reflections, inward deliberations', not 'desires' which suggests passions.
problems.ruling: ἐνθυμήσεων means 'reflections, inward deliberations'; 'desires' misleads by suggesting passions.

edits.old: For he is the searcher of thoughts and desires.
edits.new: For he is the searcher of thoughts and reflections.

fixed: Changed 'desires' to 'reflections' in both the English and the literal gloss to match the source term 'ἐνθυμήσεων' (thoughts, reflections, inward deliberations).

polish.changed: Clarified the implied speaker as God throughout, replaced the harsh 'set our wives straight' with 'guide our wives toward what is good,' and kept 'elders' consistent with the glossary while preserving 'leaders' as a distinct general term for those in authority.

notes.why: Same church offices rendered with different English words across sections.
notes.fix: Use consistent terms or add notes identifying equivalents.

notes.why: Greek terms may differ, but reader sees varying English pairs.
notes.fix: Note if these translate distinct Greek terms or are stylistic variation.

notes.quote: Let us set our wives straight toward what is good
notes.why: 'Set straight' is harsh and potentially misleading; Greek means 'guide' or 'direct.'
notes.fix: Revise to: 'Let us guide our wives in what is good.'

notes.why: The letter argues about church order, but uses 'leaders', 'elders', and 'bishops' without clear distinction, confusing the modern reader about the actual offices.
notes.fix: Add a note explaining these terms likely refer to the same office in this period.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'his' in the opening refers to God, smoothed sentence flow, and made the speaker and subject of each exhortation easier to follow without altering any claims or quotations.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὰς γυναῖκας ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀγαθὸν διορθωσώμεθα
last_rejected.why: 'διορθωσώμεθα' is 'let us correct/set straight'; 'set straight' is somewhat idiomatic but 'correct' or 'guide' would be clearer. 'Set straight' could misread as 'divorce and remarry' in modern slang. However, 'set straight' = 'correct' is still intelligible. Not clearly wrong.
last_rejected.fix: let us guide our wives toward what is good
last_rejected.ruling: διορθωσώμεθα means correct/set straight; 'set straight' is within normal range, intelligible.

last_rejected.why: 'ἀξιαγάπητον' = 'worthy of love,' not 'lovable.' 'Lovable' suggests easy to love; 'worthy of love' suggests deserving love by virtue. Different nuance.
last_rejected.fix: the character worthy of love
last_rejected.ruling: ἀξιαγάπητον = worthy of love/lovable; 'lovable' is within normal range, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: 'πραΰτης' = 'gentleness, meekness, mildness.' 'Gentleness' is within normal range. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: gentleness
last_rejected.ruling: πραΰτητος = gentleness; 'gentleness' is standard, no error.

last_rejected.why: 'ἐπιείκεια' = 'reasonableness, gentleness, forbearance, moderation.' 'Moderation' is within range. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: moderation
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπιεικὲς includes moderation; within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: how much humility prevails with God
last_rejected.why: 'τί... ἰσχύει' = 'what power/strength [it has],' not 'how much.' The sense is 'what power humility has with God' or 'how powerful humility is before God.' 'How much... prevails' captures the force adequately. Not clearly wrong.
last_rejected.fix: what power humility has with God
last_rejected.ruling: τί...ἰσχύει = what power/force; 'how much...prevails' captures sense adequately.

last_rejected.quote: how much pure love can accomplish with God
last_rejected.source_quote: τί ἀγάπη ἁγνὴ παρὰ θεῷ δύναται
last_rejected.why: Same pattern: 'τί... δύναται' = 'what power [it] has,' not 'how much... can accomplish.' 'Can accomplish' is somewhat weak; 'is able to do' or 'has power' is stronger. But 'can accomplish' is within range. Not clearly wrong.
last_rejected.fix: what power pure love has with God
last_rejected.ruling: τί...δύναται = what power; 'can accomplish' is within range.

last_rejected.source_quote: οὗ ἡ πνοὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐστίν
last_rejected.why: 'πνοή' = 'breath, spirit, wind.' 'Breath' is literal and correct. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: His breath is in us
last_rejected.ruling: πνοή = breath; 'breath' is literal and correct.

last_rejected.why: 'ἀναιρέω' = 'take away, remove, destroy, kill.' 'Take it away' for breath = 'take away life/breath.' Correct. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: he will take it away
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνελεῖ = take away/remove; 'take it away' for breath is correct.

last_rejected.source_quote: Πνεῦμα κυρίου λύχνος ἐρευνῶν τὰ ταμιεῖα τῆς γαστρός
last_rejected.why: LXX Proverbs 20:27 reads 'πνεῦμα κυρίου λύχνος ἐρευνῶν τὰ ταμιεῖα τῆς γαστρός'—this matches exactly. However, modern English Bibles number this as Proverbs 20:27 (same in Hebrew and LXX). The brief says LXX Psalm 50 = Psalm 51, but doesn't mention Proverbs numbering difference. Proverbs 20:27 is the same in both. Correct citation.
last_rejected.fix: Proverbs 20:27
last_rejected.ruling: Proverbs 20:27 matches LXX exactly; citation is correct.

last_rejected.quote: Let us consider how near he is
last_rejected.why: The Greek has 'ἴδωμεν' = 'let us see/consider' and 'πῶς ἐγγύς ἐστιν' = 'how near he is.' English captures this. Not an omission.
last_rejected.fix: Let us consider how near he is
last_rejected.ruling: ἴδωμεν πῶς ἐγγύς ἐστιν = let us see how near he is; English captures both.

last_rejected.source_quote: Πνεῦμα κυρίου λύχνος ἐρευνῶν τὰ ταμιεῖα τῆς γαστρός
last_rejected.why: The source has no explicit citation; the English adds '(Proverbs 20:27)'. This is an editorial addition, but the brief allows standard English Bible citations. However, the instruction says 'addition: English states something the source does not.' The parenthetical citation is indeed added. But is this reportable? The brief says 'Modern citations should use standard English Bible names and numbering.' This suggests adding citations is expected/allowed when the source quotes Scripture. Not an error to report.
last_rejected.fix: Πνεῦμα κυρίου λύχνος ἐρευνῶν τὰ ταμιεῖα τῆς γαστρός
last_rejected.ruling: Scripture citation added editorially; standard practice, not a real error.

last_rejected.why: LXX literal: 'storerooms of the belly.' English 'inner chambers of the belly' is idiomatic and accurate. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: inner chambers of the belly
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ ταμιεῖα = inner chambers/storerooms; 'inner chambers' is accurate idiom.

last_rejected.why: 'διαλογισμοί' = 'reasonings, deliberations, thoughts.' 'The reasonings we make' is slightly awkward but accurate. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: the reasonings we make
last_rejected.ruling: διαλογισμῶν ὧν ποιούμεθα = reasonings we make; accurate, not wrong.

last_rejected.why: 'λειποτακτέω' = 'leave one's post, desert, be absent without leave.' 'Desert his will' is metaphorical but captures 'abandon/depart from his will.' Correct. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: desert his will
last_rejected.ruling: λειποτακτεῖν = desert/leave post; 'desert his will' is correct metaphor.

last_rejected.quote: the discipline of the fear of God
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν παιδείαν τοῦ φόβου τοῦ θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: Accurate. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: the discipline of the fear of God
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν παιδείαν τοῦ φόβου = discipline of fear; accurate.

last_rejected.quote: the sincere will of their gentleness
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ ἀκέραιον τῆς πραΰτητος αὐτῶν βούλημα
last_rejected.why: Greek word order: 'the sincere/whole [thing] of their gentleness [is] will' or 'the sincere will of their gentleness.' The English parses this as 'sincere will of their gentleness' which is ambiguous—does it mean 'the will [that comes from] their gentleness' or 'their gentle will, which is sincere'? The Greek 'τὸ ἀκέραιον... βούλημα' = 'the sincere/whole will,' and 'τῆς πραΰτητος αὐτῶν' = 'of their gentleness.' So 'the sincere will [characteristic] of their gentleness.' English is accurate if slightly awkward. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: the sincere will of their gentleness
last_rejected.ruling: τὸ ἀκέραιον...βούλημα = sincere will; English parsing is accurate.

last_rejected.quote: conduct themselves in it in holiness with a pure mind
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν αὐτῷ ὁσίως ἀναστρεφομένους ἐν καθαρᾷ διανοίᾳ
last_rejected.why: 'ἐν αὐτῷ' = 'in it' (i.e., in the fear of God). 'ὁσίως ἀναστρεφομένους' = 'conducting themselves holily/in holiness.' 'ἐν καθαρᾷ διανοίᾳ' = 'with/in pure mind.' English 'conduct themselves in it in holiness with a pure mind' is accurate. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: conduct themselves in it in holiness with a pure mind
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν αὐτῷ ὁσίως ἀναστρεφομένους ἐν καθαρᾷ διανοίᾳ rendered accurately.

last_rejected.why: 'ἐρευνητής' = 'searcher, examiner, one who searches.' Correct. Not an error.
last_rejected.fix: searcher of thoughts and reflections
last_rejected.ruling: ἐρευνητὴς = searcher; correct rendering.

last_rejected.quote: Let us set our wives straight toward what is good
last_rejected.source_quote: τὰς γυναῖκας ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀγαθὸν διορθωσώμεθα
last_rejected.why: The phrase 'set our wives straight' is potentially unreadable for modern readers due to slang connotations ('set someone straight' = reprimand harshly, or 'straight' with sexual connotations). The Greek means 'correct/guide our wives toward what is good.'
last_rejected.fix: Let us guide our wives toward what is good
last_rejected.ruling: διορθωσώμεθα = set straight/correct; slang connotation is not primary meaning.

last_rejected.why: 'ἀξιαγάπητον' = 'worthy of love,' not 'lovable.' This changes the sense from 'deserving love by moral worth' to 'easy to love, attractive.'
last_rejected.fix: the character of purity worthy of love
last_rejected.ruling: ἀξιαγάπητον = worthy of love/lovable; 'lovable' within normal range, no meaning lost.
